label: prop:rigid-monoidal-structural-gap-invariance
title: Convention-independence of the structural gap: the brane-tower factors through the rigid monoidal Markov trace on the Type-B-folded Hecke category
html:
Let \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) be the rigid monoidal category. Let \tau \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) \to \mathbb{C}_q be the canonical Markov trace. Define the categorical structural gap for a confined particle \mathfrak{H} as:

  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) := B_{\mathrm{AME}}(\mathfrak{H}) - m_e \cdot \rho \cdot \bigl|\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})\bigr|.

The value \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the categorical-trace invariant \tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}). It is strictly invariant under any choice of operator-volume convention.

The Markov trace \tau is uniquely determined by the categorical axioms up to the choice of parameter z. Operator-volume conventions vary only the non-categorical regularizer. Differences in regularizer choices cancel into the identical \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} value.

The Markov trace is not invariant under the spin involution \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), \tau(\sigma_i) = q^3/(q^2+1) while \tau(\sigma_i^{-1}) = 1/\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr). That involution respects the Hecke relation only together with q \mapsto q^{-1}, and \tau is equivariant for that combined bar involution, \tau(\bar x) = \overline{\tau(x)}. So spin invariance of the LP-dual selections does not follow from properties of \tau.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It applies q-deformation identities over an abstract coefficient ring and specializes them to real-valued observables at q_0.
